title: Lay the Next Stone
prompt:
[Intro: solo piano, low strings, a choir breathing in]

[Chorus: gospel tenor at the piano, choir joining]
One day the roof goes on
I won't be there to see
So I lay the next stone
On the one she laid for me
One course higher, one day long
Lay the next stone

[Verse 1: male rap, measured, dignified]
My grandmother cleaned a building she could not walk in the front of
Saved a dollar every week inside a coffee can she wrote "for"
For what? For me. She never said it. I just know.
She died the year before I walked that stage and shook a hand, though
So I don't get to say I did it. I just got the height
She stacked beneath my feet with every floor she scrubbed at night
The ones who start it never see it. That's the deal.
You build because somebody's coming. That's what makes it real.

[Chorus: gospel tenor, choir fuller, strings]
One day the roof goes on
I won't be there to see
So I lay the next stone
On the one she laid for me
One course higher, one day long
Lay the next stone

[Verse 2: rap, rising, drums marching]
My daughter's nine, she thinks the world was always how it is
I let her think it for a minute. Let her be a kid.
Then I show her Grandma's can. It's on the kitchen shelf.
I say, "This is why you're tall. You didn't grow yourself."
She put a quarter in it. I had to leave the room.
I teach, I vote, I coach, I show up, I sweep with my own broom
I won't see what she builds. I don't need to. I can tell.
I felt it in the quarter when it fell.

[Bridge: choir alone, hands clapping slow]
Stone on stone on stone
Name on name on name
Nobody builds alone

[Final Chorus: tenor soaring, full choir and orchestra, major key]
One day the roof goes on
And we won't be there to see
So we lay the next stone
On the ones they laid for me
One course higher, one day long
Lay the next stone

[Outro: piano, one coin dropped in a can]
